entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
-
1. This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS),
2023 seeking the Court to quash the proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 & 2 in C.C.No.21 of 2025, on the file of the learned Principal Junior Civil Judge-cum- Judicial Magistrate of First Class at Madhira, registered for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.

2. Heard Sri C.Hari Preeth, learned counsel for the petitioners/accused Nos.1 & 2 as well as Sri Jitender Rao Veeramalla, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1- State.
3.

Learned petitioners' counsel has submitted that the petitioners are facing false allegations of cheating and that they have never cheated the farmers in any way and if at all there is any complaint of non-payment of amounts to the Chilli farmers, that would attract the cause of action under civil proceedings.
The present complaint is filed with an evil motive to harass the petitioners.
The ingredients of Section 420 IPC do not get attracted ETD,J Crl.P.No.14413_2025 in this case against the petitioners herein.
He therefore prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

4. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has submitted that poor farmers are being cheated by the petitioners herein and that the petitioners herein are the son and father who collected chillies from the farmers in the village at a lower price and obtained profits by selling them at higher price in the markets at several places, but had not repaid the said value to the farmers.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

The contents of the complaint point out allegations against the petitioners that they collected chillies from the farmers in the village and sold them at higher price, but the farmers were not paid their amounts.
A perusal of the charge sheet reveals that LWs 2 to 6 are listed as victims.
The truth or otherwise in the allegations shall fall for consideration during the course of trial.

6. Hence, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the Criminal Petition is disposed of dispensing with the presence of the petitioners/accused Nos.1 & 2 before the Trial Court provided that the petitioners are represented through an Advocate on every date of hearing and that they shall be present before the Trial Court ETD,J Crl.P.No.14413_2025 whenever their presence is specifically required during the course of trial.
